name: Albany Ocean Adventures
summary: Whale watching and scenic cruises out of Albany, Western Australia, hosted by skipper Paul Guest on a 19.6m catamaran. Whale watching cruises leave the town marina at 9.30am and 1pm daily from June to October, with a hydrophone on board to hear whales underwater. Scenic cruises pass historic sites around Albany and come with commentary on its maritime history.
standouts: Hydrophone on board to listen to whales underwater
19.6m aluminium catamaran with a protected viewing deck and club lounges
Full commentary from skipper Paul Guest on the whales and Albany's maritime history

contact.address: 5/A Toll Place, Albany WA (near the town marina)

trips.title: Whale Watching Tour
trips.summary: A whale watching cruise of 2.5 to 3 hours on a 19.6m catamaran, leaving Albany's new marina at 9.30am and 1pm daily from June to October, subject to numbers and weather. There is seating in club lounges with tables and on a protected viewing deck, and a hydrophone picks up whale sounds underwater. Captain Paul gives commentary on the whales and Albany's whaling history, and locally roasted coffee or tea and cake come with the cruise.
highlights: Departs 9.30am and 1pm daily in season, subject to numbers and weather
Hydrophone to listen to whales underwater
Protected viewing deck and club lounges with tables
Family friendly, with wheelchair and pram access
trips.departsFrom: Albany's new marina, off Princess Royal Drive near the town centre (booking office at 5/A Toll Place, closest to the Due South car park)
includes: Locally roasted plunger coffee or tea and chocolate or carrot cake
Hydrophone to listen to whales underwater
trips.checkNotes: PRICE CONFLICT: the Home page ticket list shows Adult $130, Seniors 120.00 (printed with no dollar sign), Children $65, Family 2+2 $350 (children 5 to 16, under 5 free). The Buy a Ticket page and the four product pages show lower prices for a 'Whale Watching Adventure': Adults $100, Seniors $90, Children $60, Family 2+2 $285, marked 'prices subject to change without prior notice'. Could not tell which is current; used the Home page because it lists every trip and the family and under 5 terms. Confirm with the operator before publishing. Booking link is the shared Rezdy catalog button (whales.rezdy.com/catalog/277735/tours) on every page, not a per-trip link; it was not opened, so product IDs and the prices and times inside it are unchecked. The Buy a Ticket page is a pay-after-booking store ('Have you booked your seat? Great! Now buy a ticket') where guests type their group size, date and time; the product pages give a booking phone number of 0428 42 9876. Duration is shown as '2.5 - 3 hours'. Departures are 'subject to numbers and weather' with no minimum number stated. Refunds are given if the trip is cancelled due to weather. 'Family 2+2' is not defined on the site beyond the children's ages. The site says payment by credit card is accepted and a PayPal account is not needed. The Home page also calls the vessel the most stable whale watching vessel of its size in WA waters, and the Whale Info and Sightings pages give sighting accounts and counts; none of these are repeated here.

trips.title: Scenic Cruises
trips.summary: A scenic cruise past the decommissioned whale chaser Cheynes II, Camp Quaranup, Point King Lighthouse and the whale museum. The skipper talks through highlights of Albany's maritime history, and the crew serve complimentary tea and coffee.
highlights: Passes the decommissioned whale chaser Cheynes II
Camp Quaranup and Point King Lighthouse
Skipper's commentary on Albany's maritime history
